summary:
Your volume has stabilised cleanly over the past eight weeks — 125 km and 127 km in back-to-back four-week blocks, 9 runs each, representing genuine consolidation rather than drift. The 20-week running streak landing exactly at your current best is worth noting: that's consistent contact with training through what appears to be a high-output period of the year, and today's 13.77 km at 5:48/km with HR 137 adds another aerobic maintenance brick without accumulating meaningful fatigue.

The standout data point in recent history remains June 27th — 15.73 km at 4:49/km with HR 161, which is your sharpest effort in this window and well inside threshold territory. Paired with today's LT test result of 4:24/km at 178 bpm, that gives you a useful anchor: your aerobic efficiency at easy effort looks solid (HR 137 for sub-6 pace), and your threshold sits at a pace consistent with someone who ran a 4:18/km half last September. There's no detraining signal here.

The 44 km long run on June 8th remains the structural foundation of the recent block — 442m of gain at 5:53/km average is meaningful durability work, and it was only three and a half weeks ago. That kind of effort takes time to express as fitness rather than fatigue, so the subsequent lower-load pattern through late June is contextually appropriate.
